title: The Squirrel and the Full Pantry

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a little red squirrel with a big fluffy tail like an umbrella and funny tufts on both ears. In an old oak, inside a cozy hollow, hides the fullest pantry of nuts in the whole forest. The hollow smells of bark, dry leaves, and forest hazelnuts. The umbrella-tail sways to and fro, as if waving hello. {name} smiles: how cozy it is here in the old oak!

Autumn gilds the forest, and {name} gathers nuts all day long. One by one, tap-tap, they drop into the little pouch. The leaves rustle under little paws: swish-swish, swish-swish. The umbrella-tail sways, and those round cheeks puff up with joy. The pouch grows heavier and heavier, and the little heart grows merrier and merrier. {name} hums a quiet autumn song.

In the evening {name} counts the treasures on the little pantry shelves. Hazelnuts, acorns, dried mushrooms — everything glows in the warm light. Little paws sort through the nuts, and they click softly, like gentle rain. Every acorn lies neatly in its place. "This is all mine," {name} thinks quietly, and the hollow feels so cozy. Outside it grows dark, while the hollow smells of mushrooms and warmth.

In the morning a soft grey rabbit friend hops to the oak, long ears drooping gently. The long ears tremble a little in the cool morning air. "Could you share just one nut?" the friend asks kindly. But {name} quietly closes the pantry door. "But these are my stores," {name} whispers softly. And somewhere deep inside, something tightens, just a tiny bit.

The rabbit shuffles away sadly, its round cottontail drooping low. {name} stays all alone beside the full pantry. Somehow the nuts no longer shine quite so warmly. The hollow grows so quiet that a little heart can be heard: thump-thump. {name} sits by the shelves and sighs softly. Even the umbrella-tail hangs a little sadly today.

The days grow shorter, and a cold wind brings the first snowflakes. {name} sits in the hollow, patting the precious stores. The wind hums its long, slow song beyond the oak's walls. {name} wraps up in the fluffy tail and listens. A full pantry, a warm hollow — it seems nothing more could be needed. Yet somehow the warm hollow feels a little too quiet today.

Then one night a great autumn storm rushes in. The wind howls, branches creak, and rain lashes down: splish-splash-splash. The old oak sways, but stands firm and strong. On the shelves the nuts roll gently to and fro. {name} curls up under the umbrella-tail and holds tight to a shelf. "Hold on, dear oak," {name} whispers into the dark.

By morning the storm has passed, and the forest stands wet and hushed. The air smells of rain and wet bark. {name} peeks from the hollow — the pantry is whole, every nut in its place. But all around come small sniffles and soft sighs. {name} perks up the tufty ears and listens very, very closely. Who can be sighing so sadly out there?

{name} climbs down and sees it: the storm has scattered everyone's stores across the whole forest. The wet leaves squelch softly under little paws. Empty little nests, washed-away hiding spots, bewildered neighbors. Some have nothing at all to eat this winter. {name} looks around, and the little heart beats fast, fast. How will the neighbors get through the winter now?

From a higher hollow peers a wise old grandmother owl in little round spectacles. The round spectacles glimmer kindly and wisely. "Your pantry is full," she says softly, "while someone near you is sad." Her voice is soft as down, not stern at all. {name} goes still and listens to those words. The words settle gently, right into the little heart.

{name} runs back into the hollow and listens to the pantry. And suddenly hears how empty a full pantry sounds when someone nearby is hungry and sad. The nuts lie quiet, as if they too are waiting. "What shall I do?" {name} asks quietly into the hush. The shelves say nothing, only smell of hazelnuts. And then the little heart whispers the answer all by itself — a warm and simple one.

Then {name} does something brand new: the pantry door swings wide open. The little door creaks softly, as if it is smiling too. First to come is the rabbit friend, and {name} pours a full handful of nuts for them. "Help yourself!" The rabbit's eyes go round with surprise, then shine like two little stars. "Thank you, thank you!" the rabbit cheers, hopping for joy.

Soon the news flies through the whole forest. A mother mouse comes in her warm little shawl with her tiny mouse-babies. The mouse-babies squeak with joy and snuggle against their mother's shawl. {name} smiles brightly and shares the nuts evenly among them all. "There is plenty for everyone — take some, don't be shy," {name} says gently. The mother mouse claps her little paws at such kindness.

Next comes the round little hedgehog neighbor, padding over the wet leaves. {name} places acorns and dried mushrooms into their paws. "What wonderful treats!" the hedgehog snuffles gratefully. The hedgehog's prickles perk right up with happiness. The pantry empties, yet the hollow grows merrier and merrier. {name} laughs brightly, and the laughter rolls through the hollow like a little nut.

The shelves grow bare, the baskets nearly empty, and yet {name} keeps smiling wider and wider. A strange thing: the fewer the nuts, the warmer the hollow feels. Each nut seems to warm twice over. {name} sorts through the last stores and hums softly. One nut for a friend, another for a neighbor, and each one carries a bit of joy along. The hollow buzzes with happy voices, like a beehive in summer.

Outside, the first real snow whirls down, white and hushed. And {name} invites everyone inside — into the warm hollow, away from the cold. "Come in, come in, there is room for everyone!" {name} calls. Snowflakes tickle the guests' noses and make them snort funnily. The rabbit, the mouse-babies, the hedgehog — all pile in together. The hollow gets a little crowded — but oh so warm.

In the hollow {name} brews a fragrant tea from red rosehips. It smells of summer, honey, and warmth. The steam rises in thin, warm little clouds. The guests warm their paws and squint with pleasure. {name} serves everyone in turn, glowing with joy. Even the wise grandmother owl comes down to warm herself and hoots gently from a corner.

Everyone settles in a circle around the warm light and nibbles nuts together. Crunch-crunch sounds merrily from every corner of the hollow. The friends smile at one another, and that makes everything taste even better. And {name} discovers a wonderful secret: nuts taste twice as good when shared with friends. {name} looks around at everyone and quietly rejoices.

Beyond the window the snow keeps falling, while inside there is laughter and quiet stories. The mouse-babies tumble, the hedgehog dozes, the rabbit hums a little song. {name} listens and feels warmth spreading inside. Little by little the voices grow softer and gentler. The mouse-babies' eyes drift sweetly shut. And beyond the window the snow falls and falls, as if tucking the forest under a fluffy blanket.

The mother mouse whispers her thanks: "You are saving our winter." {name} only smiles — something very important is clear now. The hollow smells of rosehip tea and peace. {name} takes in all this warmth with the whole of that little heart. Softly, gently, the winter evening drifts along. Kindness that is shared always comes back as warmth.

The pantry is nearly empty now, but the hollow is brimful of friends. {name} looks at them all — the rabbit, the mouse-babies, the hedgehog — and thinks this is the warmest winter ever. Some of the guests are snuffling softly already, some are yawning sweetly. The quiet in the hollow is warm, like a downy little blanket. {name} squints with quiet happiness. Empty shelves, and a heart that is full.

Outside sleeps the white, white forest beneath a starry sky. And in the warm hollow {name} curls up under the umbrella-tail among friends and yawns sweetly. Little eyes close all on their own. The breathing grows quiet and slow, quiet and slow. Friends snuffle softly nearby, and that makes sleep even sweeter. The fullest pantry is the one you share. Good night, kind little heart!
